title: bug: VS Code protected daemon provenance tests flake under full-suite load with 25ms stop deadlines
description:
During task-d5eca150 verification at base 66f43585, Linux npm test failed only '(7) replace succeeds' and 'cancel during stop' with protected admission refusals; unchanged rerun passed 685/676/0/9, and the isolated provenance file passed 47/47.
The fixture in moe-vscode/tests/protected-daemon-provenance.test.cjs sets both replacement deadlines to 25ms while its fake stop exit uses setImmediate, allowing full-suite scheduling delay to win. Logs: /tmp/d5eca150-linux.x3fOok/{verification.log,verification-rerun.log,provenance-rerun.log}. Stabilize test scheduling without weakening fail-closed coverage or changing production behavior.
definitionOfDone: Successful-stop and stop-cancellation rows are deterministic under full-suite load while timeout/failure rows still test refusal.
moe-vscode npm test && npm run compile passes in Linux and Windows full-repo snapshots.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix the fake stop child's scheduling in moe-vscode/tests/protected-daemon-provenance.test.cjs. It is the only file this task changes: edit it with the Edit tool, never a shell write. moe-vscode/src stays byte-identical. Read mem:gotcha-vscode-provenance-test-deadlines first.
Why it flakes: loadClient's fake spawn answers the installed stop on setImmediate. MoeDaemonClient.stopProtectedDaemon arms setTimeout(kill + finish(false), replaceStopTimeoutMs = 25) right after spawn() returns. An immediate queued from a check-phase callback runs only after the next timers phase. A stall of 25 ms or more under full-suite load therefore lets the deadline kill and refuse a stop that succeeded.
(a) RED first, in scratch only:
- From the task worktree: X=$(mktemp -d /tmp/787437bb-red.XXXXXX); git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$X". Archive the whole tree (mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot).
- In "$X/moe-vscode" run npm ci --no-audit --no-fund under the same env -i HOME/PATH (nvm node v24.21.0) as checkRef [0].
- Write "$X/defer-immediate.cjs" containing exactly the one line: globalThis.setImmediate = (fn, ...args) => setTimeout(fn, 30, ...args);
  It simulates load: every immediate waits behind a 30 ms timer, so a 25 ms deadline armed after it fires first.
- From "$X/moe-vscode" run: node --require ../defer-immediate.cjs tests/protected-daemon-provenance.test.cjs
  Expected, architect-validated at 5f731334: exit 1, tests 47 / pass 38 / fail 9. The failing rows are exactly: (7) replace succeeds; (8) replace fails closed: nonzero, ENOENT, alive, new pid, unreadable, oversize; cancel during stop; replacement must verify the fresh daemon rather than trusting its spawn.
- Without --require the file passes 47/47.
- Keep the logs.
(b) The fix, in loadClient's fake spawn:
- Replace `setImmediate(() => {` with `(args[1].includes('stop') ? process.nextTick : setImmediate)(() => {`.
- The stop outcome then arrives on process.nextTick: the exit with f.stopCode, the ENOENT error, or nothing for hang. That queue drains before the event loop can run any timer, so the outcome always precedes the 25 ms stop deadline. Only the hang row reaches that deadline.
- The start child's 'spawn' and StubWebSocket's 'open' stay on setImmediate. No short production timer races them.
- Add a two-line comment above the call saying this; Node itself delivers a spawn error on process.nextTick.
- Keep these byte-identical: the callback body, client.replaceStopTimeoutMs = client.replaceExitTimeoutMs = 25; client.replacePollMs = 2;, every row and every assertion.
- Expected diff: 1 file, about +3/-1.
(c) GREEN in the same scratch tree:
- cp the edited file over $X's copy, then cmp them.
- The --require run must exit 0 with 47/47 (Windows: 45 pass, 2 POSIX-only skips).
- The plain run must also pass 47/47.
(d) Show that the timeout/failure rows still test refusal:
- Mutate only $X/moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts. After each mutant, restore it from git show HEAD:moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and cmp it.
- MA: delete the try { child.kill(); } catch { ... } statement in stopProtectedDaemon's timer callback. Exactly '(8) replace fails closed: hang' must fail.
- MB: insert if (pid) { return true; } as the first statement of waitForReplacementExit. Exactly (8) alive, new pid, unreadable and oversize must fail.
- Both are architect-validated. Record the logs.
Error handling: no production error handling changes. The fixture still emits the ENOENT 'error' that stopProtectedDaemon's error listener turns into a refusal, and the t.after cleanup is unchanged. Delete only your own mktemp dirs, case-guarded on the /tmp/787437bb-red. prefix.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: deliver the fake stop child's outcome on process.nextTick. That queue drains before the event loop can run any timer, so the exit or error always beats the 25 ms stop deadline. The ordering is deterministic by construction, with no wall-clock margin.
Rejected:
(1) Raise the deadlines for the success rows only (for example 60 s). It keeps a wall-clock race behind setImmediate. A regression would hang the run for the full deadline. It also leaves the same race in the (8) rows' f.killed === (mode === 'hang') assertion and in the 'replacement must verify' spawn count, which the forced-delay repro also fails.
(2) Fake timers in the vm sandbox. This rewires every row's timing for no gain.
(3) A permanent in-file row that patches globalThis.setImmediate. It tests the test and mutates a global inside a shared file. Instead the verification command carries the deferred-setImmediate run, so QA re-checks determinism on both OSes.
(4) Changing production deadlines or adding a test hook. Out of scope (DoD 1, governor placement note).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Race: stopProtectedDaemon arms setTimeout(kill + finish(false), replaceStopTimeoutMs) right after spawn(). The fixture overrides replaceStopTimeoutMs to 25. The fake stop answers on setImmediate. An immediate queued from a check-phase callback runs only in the next loop iteration, after that iteration's timers phase. With a stall of 25 ms or more (parallel node --test files transpiling TypeScript, GC), the deadline wins.
Forced repro: a --require preload setting globalThis.setImmediate = (fn, ...args) => setTimeout(fn, 30, ...args). At 5f731334 the same 9 rows fail on Linux node 24.21 (38 pass) and on native Windows node (36 pass, 2 skipped): (7); (8) nonzero, ENOENT, alive, new pid, unreadable, oversize; cancel during stop; replacement must verify. With the one-line fix: 47/47 on Linux and 45 + 2 skipped on Windows, with and without the preload. Mutants MA (no kill on the stop deadline) and MB (exit wait returns true) were killed by exactly the intended rows.
